subject: oop
question: Checked vs unchecked exceptions in Java with examples.
title: Gate Scan or Mid-Flight
hook: Some bags are scanned at the gate. Other problems only show up mid-flight.
answer: Checked exceptions: checked by the compiler at compile time; the code will not compile unless you handle them (try-catch) or declare them (throws). Usually external problems. Examples: IOException, FileNotFoundException, SQLException.
Unchecked exceptions: subclasses of RuntimeException; NOT checked at compile time, so handling is optional; the problem appears at run time; usually programming bugs.
Key difference: checked = compiler forces you to handle or declare; unchecked = compiler stays silent and it crashes at run time.
